title: Draft + socialize PRD for Standard Cost Model Spec & API (v1 scope + success metrics)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
We need a single PRD that sets v1 scope and a shared definition of “inference cost” so Console dashboards and Optimize ROI estimates stop diverging across telemetry, billing hooks, and ad-hoc models.

This ticket covers:
- Drafting the Standard Cost Model PRD (problem, goals/non-goals, v1 scope, phased rollout)
- Socializing with stakeholders (Platform, Telemetry, Runtime, Console, Optimize, SRE, Finance)
- Capturing decisions + open questions (especially breakdown taxonomy + overhead allocation)
- Defining measurable success metrics + acceptance criteria for “v1 shipped”

Out of scope for this PM ticket: implementing endpoints/schemas (tracked in ENG tickets).
problem_statement:
Today we have inconsistent cost numbers and semantics across:
- Console cost breakdown views (observability)
- Optimize “what-if” savings estimates
- Telemetry aggregation and attribution
- Billing hooks / invoicing primitives

Common failure modes:
- Prefill vs decode token accounting differs between runtime metrics and downstream aggregation
- Cache hits and batch efficiency are represented differently across teams (units/definitions)
- Quantization impacts (throughput/memory/quality constraints) aren’t modeled consistently
- Overhead allocation is treated inconsistently (request-attributable vs pooled costs)

Result: Customers and internal teams can’t trust cost breakdowns; support escalations occur when Console does not match invoice totals or when ROI claims appear inflated.
goals: Publish a v1 PRD that defines canonical cost semantics and the minimum fields/endpoints needed for Console + Optimize adoption in Q1 2026.
Align on a versioned spec + API approach (owned by Platform) with backward compatibility rules.
Define how standardized cost outputs map to finance/unit economics reporting (including overhead allocation policy and reporting windows).
Set measurable success criteria (latency budget, drift tolerances, adoption milestones, supportability).
non_goals: Replacing billing/RevRec systems (cost model is not the system of record for invoicing).
Shipping a customer-facing pricing calculator in v1.
Perfectly modeling every hardware SKU/edge case in v1; we will define an extension path (v2+) with explicit versioning.
v1_scope_must_haves: Canonical cost breakdown taxonomy for v1 (prefill vs decode; cache attribution; batching efficiency; overhead allocation category).
Versioned schema package (inputs/outputs) with deterministic semantics (same inputs => same outputs).
Internal Cost Model API endpoints for: per-request estimate, aggregated breakdown (bounded), and limited what-if projections for config changes.
Schema version negotiation guidance for clients (Console/Optimize) and deprecation rules.
Telemetry input contracts: required runtime + metering fields, units, and data quality checks.
Rollout plan with feature flags, fallback behavior, and validation dashboards (predicted vs observed spend drift).
v1_scope_nice_to_haves: Confidence intervals for what-if projections (where data supports it) and explicit ‘assumptions’ surfaced in response metadata.
Region/SKU-level overhead breakdown for finance drill-down (may be v2 depending on data availability).
Self-serve debugging UI for internal support to compare invoice vs standardized primitives.
personas_and_use_cases:
Console (Chloe/Jada/Felix):
- Show cost breakdown by route/model/customer/workspace for dashboards.
- Must be fast for hot paths; requires bounded payloads and caching guidance.

Optimize (Aditya/Maya/Jonas):
- Compute ROI of recommendations (batching, caching, quantization) using a what-if endpoint.
- Must include guardrails (parameter bounds, assumptions) to avoid optimistic or misleading estimates.

Finance/FP&A (Laura/Rishi):
- Consume standardized primitives to improve unit economics reporting consistency.
- Needs stability across reporting windows + explicit overhead allocation policy.

SRE/Platform:
- Operate a reliable internal service with SLOs and drift monitoring; manage schema version distribution.
success_metrics:
Product metrics:
- Console cost breakdown pages powered by Cost Model API for >= 80% of workspaces within 2 weeks of GA (behind feature flag initially).
- Optimize ROI calculations for batching/caching/quantization using standardized outputs for >= 90% of recommendations shown to users (excluding explicitly unsupported models).

Quality metrics:
- Drift SLI: aggregated predicted cost vs observed spend within agreed tolerance band for stable workloads (initial target: within 5–10% weekly, with documented exclusions for telemetry lag and known gaps).
- Support: reduce cost mismatch tickets tagged “Console vs invoice” by 50% within 1 quarter post-launch.

Operational metrics:
- API p95 latency within budget for Console hot path (target to be set in design spec; PRD proposes p95 <= 150ms for cached/steady-state estimate calls, <= 400ms for uncached within bounded inputs).
- Error rate within SLO target (tbd by SRE) and automatic fallback behavior does not degrade Console UX.
acceptance_criteria_v1:
PRD is considered complete when:
1) The PRD is published in Confluence and reviewed/approved (explicit +1) by Platform, Telemetry, Console, Optimize, SRE, and Finance stakeholders.
2) v1 breakdown taxonomy is written unambiguously with examples (what counts as prefill vs decode, how cache hits are attributed, what overhead categories exist).
3) v1 endpoint list and required fields are defined (even if exact schema is finalized in ENG-4822).
4) v1 rollout plan is defined: feature flags, staging validation, canary/rollback conditions, and ownership.
5) Open questions are documented with owners and dates for resolution (no unresolved “blocking” items).

Launch readiness criteria (to be verified later during implementation):
- Conformance tests/golden fixtures exist for core computations.
- Drift dashboard exists and is reviewed with SRE + Finance.
- Console and Optimize integration plans have explicit fallback behavior if API is degraded.

open_questions: Overhead allocation: exact categories and whether overhead is returned as a separate component or folded into unit costs (owner: Laura Bennett + Ethan Park).
Drift definition: what is the ‘observed’ comparator (GPU spend by pool? amortized commitments?) and what exclusions apply (owner: Rafael Mendes + Rishi Malhotra).
Cache attribution: how to attribute shared KV cache benefits across requests (owner: Omar El-Sayed + Nadia Rahman).
What-if warm cache assumption: whether to include a cache warm-rate input in v1 or defer to v2 (owner: Jonas Weber + Ethan Park).
Bounding: max number of breakdown dimensions returned per query for Console (owner: Jada Williams + Thomas Baird).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Cardinality blowups for aggregated breakdown endpoints.
Mitigation: Enforce strict request bounds; provide top-K + ‘other’ buckets; require time window constraints; pre-aggregation where needed.

Risk: Console performance regression due to synchronous dependency.
Mitigation: Provide caching guidance + client library; require fallbacks to existing estimates when service is degraded; stage rollout behind feature flags.

Risk: Drift alerts fire due to telemetry lag, causing low trust in system.
Mitigation: Define lag-aware SLIs; add lag signals to dashboards; use backfill for comparisons; document expected lag.

Risk: Optimize ROI claims become misleading due to optimistic assumptions.
Mitigation: Guardrails + bounded parameter ranges; surface assumptions and confidence; require conservative defaults.

Risk: Finance reporting instability due to schema/semantics changes.
Mitigation: Versioned schema, explicit deprecation windows, and release notes tied to reporting windows.
rollout_plan_summary:
Phase 1 (Discovery): inventory current definitions; confirm Console/Optimize v1 requirements; agree on minimal v1 fields.
Phase 2 (Spec): publish schema semantics + ADRs; finalize breakdown taxonomy and overhead policy.
Phase 3 (Implementation): ship service/library + conformance tests.
Phase 4 (Integration): Console + Optimize behind flags; validate against drift dashboards; run backtests.
Phase 5 (Launch): expand flag rollout; publish governance docs and runbooks; begin deprecation of legacy cost paths.
